name: Maggie Hassan

statements.quote: Although there has been considerable Congressional attention paid to many of the public safety risks posed by artificial intelligence, there has been less focus on so-called ‘catastrophic’ risks posed by AI – such as the ability of AI to help terrorists develop and use unconventional weapons [...] I’m working on a framework to support research into safer AI that – in its fundamental design – cannot easily be abused by criminals and cannot easily behave in unexpected ways that would harm the public. Congress needs to look closely at ways to require AI to be designed in a fundamentally safer way, and – in time – require all AI hardware to be restricted to running only fundamentally safe systems.
statements.venue: Remarks at Senate Emerging Threats subcommittee hearing, via press release

statements.quote: There is growing concern among workers in many industries that AI can fundamentally change the nature of work in unpredictable ways, […] do you have recommendations for how the federal government should be addressing challenges that companies and employees face from the use of AI in the workplace?
statements.venue: Question at Senate Homeland Security Committee AI hearing, via press release

statements.quote: As artificial intelligence advances rapidly, we must work on a bipartisan basis to proactively address the potential national security threats posed by this technology. [...] We must continue to work to protect against potential risks to public safety, such as the misuse of this technology by terrorists or criminal organizations. By implementing balanced oversight of the most advanced AI models, we can maintain our technological leadership while protecting public safety and our national interests.
statements.venue: Press release on introducing the Preserving American Dominance in AI Act

statements.quote: As AI technology continues to advance rapidly, we need to make sure that these systems are secure and that they make reliable decisions. This bipartisan bill invests in research that makes AI harder to manipulate and easier to predict, so that we can also strengthen our defenses against bad actors and foreign adversaries like China, who may utilize AI to hurt Americans.
statements.venue: Press release on Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act

statements.quote: American workers cannot be left behind as American corporations continue to push forward with the development and adoption of artificial intelligence. This bipartisan legislation helps the federal government better assess the ways in which artificial intelligence is changing our economy and helps ensure that increased automation does not result in fewer jobs for hard-working American families.
statements.venue: Press release on AI Workforce PREPARE Act

statements.quote: In recent years, global criminal networks have used deepfake voice programs, along with other new AI tools, to target more people with increasingly personalized and believable digital scams, fueling a booming scam industry that surpasses the global drug trade as an illicit industry [...] Protecting Americans from these financial losses will require collaboration between the public and private sectors, and AI companies [including yours] are on the frontlines of this effort.
statements.venue: Letters to AI voice cloning companies, via JEC press release

statements.quote: I write today to request information about what immediate and long-term steps Hugging Face will take to address the reported use of your technology to easily create deepfake sexual content of women and children.
statements.venue: Letter to Hugging Face CEO, via JEC press release

statements.quote: Our government’s number one job is to keep people safe. That work involves protecting against terrorism and fentanyl trafficking, but it also includes guarding against emerging threats like artificial intelligence security risks and strengthening our cybersecurity.

raw:
Let me look for more: the Banks AI security bill, the Hugging Face letter, extreme risks bill, and chatbots.I found eight statements by Sen. Hassan about AI. All are her own words from her Senate press releases, a joint committee site or a news article. I could not find interviews, floor speeches, op-eds or social media posts with usable exact quotes. I left out joint letters she co-signed, such as the Hassan–Hawley and Hassan–Ernst letters, because I couldn't attribute the wording to her alone. I also left out the Meta tax-credit letter, whose quoted passages weren't about AI.
